content.content:
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
}

export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
}

/**
 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
 */
export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
  const user = await realUser();
  if (!user) redirect("/login");
  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
  return user;
}

I'm leaning toward audit being visible to any role that can access at least one tab, but restricting settings edits to platform, and keeping build visibility (which includes customer prompts) limited to fleet since it's sensitive. The nav tabs themselves should be filtered by these same permission checks, which gives me clean, testable logic.

For the abuse-flags-and-rate-limits tab, I'm realizing a per-user block control would need to hook into the shared createModBuild logic to actually be enforced, which goes beyond just adding admin-only pages and adapters.

I'm thinking the cleanest approach is a single Cyrus suspension mechanism stored in a Setting (a JSON list of suspended users with reason, duration, and who issued it), scoped to either "build" or "community" so it covers both blocking new builds and blocking posting/publishing — tying together this tab and the creator-suspensions tab. Enforcement would just be a minimal one-line check inserted into createModBuild and into the community actions file, keeping the merge risk low even though it touches files owned by other agents. For the rate-limit display itself, I want to show each user's 24h usage against their daily cap, their in-flight builds against the max of 2, and their builds in the last hour against the 20/hour limit.

For abuse flags, I want to derive these heuristically from real data rather than invent anything — refused-build counts over 30 days, safety block findings, reports against posts, and high failure rates — wrapped in a pure, testable `abuseSignals()` function so it stays honest and grounded.

For the games settings override, I'm realizing the client-safe games data needs a server-side companion that reads settings and computes an effective games list, merging overrides into the base config. =================== capabilities
# Brief: capabilities: safe mod networking

Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/CONTEXT.md` first (shared rules; node-2 sharing rules apply: one dev server fleet-wide, heavy runs under the lock). Then read the efficiency agent's work: branch `feature/cyrus-v6-efficiency` (service 0.5), its notes `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/efficiency/EFFICIENCY.md`, and the research `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/research/ADVANCED-MODS.md`. Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-capabilities -b feature/cyrus-v6-capabilities feature/cyrus-v6-efficiency`. Notes: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/capabilities/`.

## Context: the owner's decision (2026-10-08)
The Minecraft build service's safety scan currently hard-blocks ALL networking. The owner said: "loosen. Maybe some networking is possible for the advancement of mod creation." This is the main ceiling on advanced mods (web APIs, Discord/webhook integrations, remote config, economy and voting services, AI-driven NPCs). Nxeon has had serious security incidents (a platform RCE, a cryptominer from a framework bug), so loosen **safely and by design, not by deleting the rule**.

## Your scope: a capability model for mod networking
1. **Threat model first** (`THREAT-MODEL.md`): what a malicious or careless generated plugin could do with network access (data exfiltration of player/IP/config data, downloading and executing code, class-loading remote jars, reverse shells, SSRF into the customer's own network or the Nxeon internal network, crypto mining, DoS from the server, credential theft, blocking the main thread), and which of those each control stops.
2. **Design**: mods may only use the network through a vetted Nxeon wrapper (`NxHttp`: a small, audited helper class the build service injects into every plugin's classpath/shade), never raw `java.net`, `HttpClient`, sockets, URLClassLoader or reflection around it. The wrapper enforces: HTTPS only, a **declared host allow-list in the plugin manifest** (`nx-capabilities.yml`: hosts, purpose, reads/writes player data yes/no), resolved-IP checks blocking private/loopback/link-local/metadata ranges (anti-SSRF, including after redirects and DNS rebinding), async only (never on the server thread), request/response size and time limits, rate limits, no custom headers that smuggle secrets, a User-Agent identifying Cyrus, logging of every outbound call, and a kill switch via config.
3. **Scanner changes** in the service (`scan.js`, `precheck.js`, rules): replace "block all networking" with "block direct networking APIs; allow only the wrapper with a manifest-declared allow-list"; keep blocking process execution, native loading, remote class loading, `Runtime.exec`, file access outside the plugin folder, reflection that reaches around the wrapper, obfuscation, and anything else already blocked. Add tests with adversarial examples (string-built URLs, reflection, `Class.forName`, ScriptEngine, JNDI, `ProcessBuilder`, DNS exfil via `InetAddress`).
4. **Customer consent and visibility**: the install flow (and the listing page, `Explain` data and NxLabs page) shows "This mod connects to: hosts, for: purposes, and can/cannot send player data"; installation requires an explicit confirm; the manifest is part of the build metadata (`MbFinding`/meta in `lib/modbuilder/types.ts`). Add the pure helpers in `lib/cyrus/capabilities.ts` (types, validation, summary text) and the UI hooks as small additive components (the lifecycle agent owns the install dialog: expose a `CapabilityConsent` component and tell them the contract).
5. **AI features without arbitrary networking (design, behind a flag)**: for LLM-driven NPCs or AI chat in mods, the plugin never talks to a model provider directly. It calls a **Nxeon AI gateway** endpoint (design the API: per-server token, metered in tokens through the existing economy, rate limits, moderation, prompt-injection and abuse controls, no secrets in the mod). Write the design and the minimal gateway stub; do not build the model plumbing.
6. **Roll-out plan**: phases, kill switches (per mod, per customer, global setting), admin visibility (which published mods declare networking), review queue for community mods that declare networking, and what the owner must approve before enabling (default OFF; a setting `cyrus_mod_networking_enabled`).
7. Do NOT deploy, do NOT touch VM 88001, and run no real outbound network from tests (use local fixtures). Deliver the patch to `services/modbuilder/` on your branch with install notes (next service version, rollback), unit tests and a clean `devhost tsc`.

Finish with a short report: the threat model's residual risks, what you recommend the owner approve, and an honest statement of what could only be verified against a real build.
=================== library
# Brief: library: the verified Cyrus pattern library

Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/CONTEXT.md` first (shared rules; node-2 sharing rules apply: one dev server fleet-wide, heavy runs under the lock). Then read the efficiency agent's work: branch `feature/cyrus-v6-efficiency` (service 0.5), its notes `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/efficiency/EFFICIENCY.md`, and the research `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/research/ADVANCED-MODS.md`. Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-library -b feature/cyrus-v6-library feature/cyrus-v6-efficiency`. Notes: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/library/`.

## Context: the owner's question (2026-10-08)
"Maybe create massive mod creation libraries with tons of trained, trialed and tested data that can be utilised for mod creation, whilst also keeping the mod generation cheap. Do you think it's worth it to train Cyrus on other pre-created mods?" The coordinator's answer: do NOT fine-tune and do NOT scrape other people's mods (licences, platform terms, and fine-tuning is not available for the models used). Build a **verified pattern library** instead, used through retrieval into the cached prompt prefix.

## Your scope: the Cyrus Pattern Library (Minecraft first, generic schema)
1. **Policy first** (`LICENSING-POLICY.md`): which sources are allowed (permissively licensed example projects such as MIT/Apache/MIT-0 official examples, the platform docs' own samples where the licence permits, Nxeon-authored patterns, and Cyrus's OWN successful builds), which are not (anything all-rights-reserved or GPL being copied, bulk scraping Modrinth/CurseForge/Spigot/GitHub in violation of terms, community mods without the author's explicit opt-in). Verify each source's licence by reading it; record SPDX id, URL, commit and attribution requirements in the pattern metadata. For customer builds, design an **explicit opt-in** (listing setting) before a build can become a library pattern, plus removal on request.
2. **Schema** (`lib/cyrus/library/types.ts`, JSON next to the service like the knowledge packs so the Node service can read it): a pattern = id, title, category (the universal categories from `lib/cyrus/categories.ts`/routing agent), description, the code (small, focused: a command, config load/save, listener, scheduler task, GUI, economy hook, scoreboard, placeholders, database access...), dependencies, the **verification record** (game, version(s), loader, build/compile result, runtime load result, date, tool versions), source and licence, and a content hash. Patterns are distilled building blocks, not whole mods.
3. **Pipeline**: ingest from the allowed sources (start with the permissive examples and Paper API docs examples already in the repo/service sheets; mine the service's own passing evals under `services/modbuilder/eval`, read-only), normalise, **compile-verify each pattern against each supported version** with the service's toolchain (on node-2, Paper API jars are public: see how the service gets them; no proprietary files), and write the verification record. A scheduled re-verify script reruns the library against a new game version and flags patterns that stop compiling or loading, feeding the lifecycle agent's out-of-date logic (expose `lib/cyrus/library/status.ts`).
4. **Retrieval and cost**: design and implement how patterns reach the model cheaply: a compact pattern index in the cached prefix, the model asks for/gets only the patterns for the planned features (by category and feature tags, deterministic first), measured against **CloudAPIBench's warning that retrieval can hurt common APIs**: so run an A/B on the existing eval set (offline cost model unless you can run it safely; you may run at most 6 real builds in total, and only through a path that does not touch VM 88001's production role; otherwise report a design with predicted effects and say so). Report token and cost deltas and the first-try pass rate impact, honestly.
5. **Scale plan**: how to grow it from a few dozen patterns to thousands: contributor workflow, review and test gates, deduplication, per-version maintenance burden, storage and size limits, and a quality bar (a pattern must compile on every claimed version and load on a real Paper server in the harness before it is `verified`). Include the "learning loop": each successful, opted-in customer build proposes new patterns; failures update the failure rules (the knowledge packs the game agents are building in `GameSupport.knowledge`; align with their shape and the efficiency agent's `export-knowledge.js`).
6. Seed at least 25 verified Minecraft patterns you can fully justify licence-wise (Nxeon-authored ones are fine, written fresh by you and verified), with the tooling to add more. Do NOT deploy and do NOT touch VM 88001.

Finish with a short report: library size, verification coverage, measured or modelled effect on cost and quality, licensing decisions the owner must confirm, and what you recommend next.
=================== lifecycle
# Brief: lifecycle: install, enable/disable, health, updates, creator warnings

Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/CONTEXT.md` first (the owner's full request, the shared rules, the roster). Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-lifecycle -b feature/cyrus-v6-lifecycle feature/cyrus-v6`. Output dir for notes: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/lifecycle/`.

## Your scope
Read first: `lib/cyrus-mods/installed.ts`, `lib/actions-cyrus-installed.ts`, `lib/modbuilder/install.ts`, the `ServerMod` model and the `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job path (`worker/`), the game panel's mods tab, `lib/prefs.ts` (notification kinds), and the GameSupport contract `lib/cyrus/games/support.ts` (the game agents will fill it in; code against the type).

Build a complete **mod lifecycle on customers' own servers**:
1. **Install**: from Cyrus and from NxLabs onto a chosen server, per game using `GameSupport.install` (path, packaging, restart needed, hot reload, and, for games where players need the mod too, a clear plain-language "players must also install this" step with instructions). Version-compatibility check before install (block on unsupported, warn on legacy), a confirm step with the warnings, a backup of the previous mod file and config, and automatic rollback if the install job fails.
2. **Enable / disable** without deleting (move to a disabled folder or loader-specific switch, per game), with states: Enabled, Disabled, Pending restart, Failed, Broken, Outdated. Config is preserved.
3. **Health and warnings**: detect **broken** (loader errors naming the mod in the server log, using per-game patterns from `GameSupport.outdatedSignals`/a log-pattern list you define; crash loop right after an install triggers auto-disable and a notification) and **out of date** (game/loader moved past the mod's tested range, or a newer version exists). Show warnings in the portal: badge on the mod row and server card, banner on the server page, and optional email through the existing notification-preference gate (add a NON-critical kind in `lib/prefs.ts`).
4. **Updating**: one-click update to a newer version of the same mod, config kept, changelog shown, rollback; "Update all"; per-mod opt-in auto-update.
5. **Creator warnings**: when a game/loader version change makes a published mod likely stale, or several installed copies report errors, warn the **mod's creator** ("your mod may need an update for Minecraft 1.21.5") in the portal and by email, deduped and rate-limited, with a one-click "Update with Cyrus for the new version" that opens the project with the version preselected (the refine path; keep the cost low). Implement the detector as a worker sweep that is **inert until enabled** by a setting (`cyrus_compat_watch_enabled`, default off), reading versions from `GameSupport` and live server data, with a dry-run mode that only logs.
6. All server writes go through the existing job system. **Never touch real customer servers in dev**: use mocks and the throwaway DB.

## Verify
Pure tests for the state machine and warning rules; mock-driven end-to-end of install, disable, broken detection (feed sample logs), update and creator warning; real server-rendered screens with screenshots (mods tab states, warnings, update dialog, creator warning), dark + light, 1440 + 390; `devhost tsc` clean; docs with the state diagram.
=================== community
# Brief: community: NxLabs hand-off, remixing and community versions

Read `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/CONTEXT.md` first (the owner's full request, the shared rules, the roster). Worktree: `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-community -b feature/cyrus-v6-community feature/cyrus-v6`. Output dir for notes: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/community/`.

## Your scope
Read first: `lib/cyrus-mods/*` (community.ts, doc.ts, pages.ts, registry.ts, installed.ts, gate.ts), `lib/actions-cyrus-mods.ts`, the NxLabs mod store pages (`grep -rn "nxlabs" app components lib -il`), the Prisma models behind them, `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v4/` and the memory note `nxeon-ai-modbuilder.md`. Understand what already exists (threads of NOTE/BUG/FIX, reports, versions, installs) before adding.

The owner's vision (verbatim in CONTEXT.md): Cyrus is a **community**. A Cyrus project can be opened in **NxLabs**, where the creator changes the title, adds photos and fully customises the mod page. Other people can **build off** a mod, can **load other community Cyrus mods directly into their own Cyrus**, and **their changes go under "Community versions" on the original mod's page**. "I really want you to expand on this community idea."

Build:
1. **Open in NxLabs**: from a Cyrus mod, one click to its listing; an owner edit mode there for title, icon/banner, **photo gallery**, long description (markdown, reuse the existing renderer/sanitiser), tags, links, changelog, visibility. Own the storage and `saveModListing(projectIdOrBuildId, input)` + the shared type from `lib/cyrus/listing.ts` (the routing agent defines `ModListingInput`; if not on your branch yet, define a compatible type in `lib/cyrus-mods/listing.ts` and note it).
2. **Remix / build on**: authors choose whether remixing is allowed (sensible default, documented), with credit ("Remixed from X by Y") preserved down the chain. "Remix in my Cyrus" creates a new project seeded with the source and prompt history. The remix's published versions appear under **Community versions** on the ORIGINAL page (a list with author, base version, summary, diff view using `lib/cyrus/diff.ts`, test status); the original author can pin/endorse one. Re-scan remixed code through the existing safety scanner before any build.
3. **Load community mods into my Cyrus**: a library/"Add to my Cyrus" action puts a community mod on my map as a read-only branch node (installable, remixable) without copying it until I remix.
4. **Expand the community**, in order of value, implementing the core and leaving a clear roadmap for the rest: stars/likes; creator profiles; collections ("modpacks"); a computed, objective **Community-tested** status that earns the laurel badge (define criteria from real data: installs, ratings, no open BUG, works on the current game version; never manual or fake); "works with version X" compatibility tags; changelogs; fork graph view; report/moderation hooks (reuse the existing report flow). Every number shown is real. Use `BuiltWithCyrusBadge` from the studio-ui agent (`components/cyrus/brand/`); if absent when you need it, create it under `components/cyrus-mods/` with the same props and note the duplicate for the merge.
5. **Schema**: you own Prisma additions for all of this: additive only, new tables or nullable/defaulted columns, no new unique constraint on populated tables, placed at the end of the file with comments. Include a migration note and the exact `db push` expectation.

## Verify
Throwaway DB on node-2 with seeded demo mods and users (clearly fake), real server-rendered NxLabs pages and the Cyrus actions, screenshots (listing editor, photos, remix flow, community versions list, library, laurel badge), dark + light, 1440 + 390, `devhost tsc` clean, tests for the pure rules (criteria, remix permissions, credit chain).

# Cyrus × Rust: readiness and how Rust modding works

Agent: game-rust (Cyrus v6). Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-rust`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-game-rust`.
Research date: 2026-10-08. Current Rust build: **2634.289.1** (October 2026 forced update, 1 Oct). Next forced update: **Thu 5 Nov 2026, 19:00 UTC**.

Rust stays **`soon`** in `lib/cyrus/games.ts`. Making it `live` is the owner's call. The list below is what's still missing.

---

## Part 1: How Rust modding works (one page, also usable on the marketing page)

**A Rust mod is a server plugin.** It's one C# source file (`MyPlugin.cs`). The server compiles it, so you don't build it first. Two frameworks run these plugins:

- **Oxide (uMod).** The long-standing standard, MIT open source. It ships patched copies of the game's server DLLs. Plugins live in `oxide/plugins`, settings in `oxide/config`, saved data in `oxide/data`, translations in `oxide/lang`, logs in `oxide/logs`.
- **Carbon.** A newer framework that runs the same Oxide plugins unchanged. Instead of shipping patched DLLs it patches the game at runtime, and it uses `carbon/plugins` and similar folders. Oxide and Carbon can't be installed on the same server. Nxeon offers Oxide today. Carbon isn't offered yet.

**Install and reload.** Drop the `.cs` file into the plugins folder. Within seconds the framework compiles it (Roslyn, C# 14) and loads it. Edit the file and it hot-reloads. No restart, no downtime. On first load the plugin writes its own config file, and you edit that to tune it.

**Players install nothing.** Rust has no client modding: the game client is protected by Easy Anti-Cheat and has no mod loader. Plugins still change a lot of what players experience:
- menus, HUDs and overlays (CUI, drawn by the server and sent to each player),
- chat commands and messages,
- custom versions of existing items (renamed, re-skinned with Steam Workshop skins, given new behaviour),
- spawned NPCs, vehicles, crates and events,
- gather rates, loot, crafting, raid rules and weather.

They can't add new 3D models, textures or sounds that aren't already in the game.

**How a plugin plugs in.** The framework calls named methods ("hooks") when things happen in the game: `OnEntityTakeDamage` when something is hit, `OnPlayerInput` on key presses, `OnLootSpawn` when a crate fills, and so on. There are about 737 hooks today. A hook that returns a value can cancel the game's action, for example blocking damage.

**Permissions** follow `<plugin>.<permission>` (for example `frostaxe.use`) and are granted with `oxide.grant group default frostaxe.use`.

**The monthly cycle (the main reason plugins break).** Facepunch ships a forced update on the **first Thursday of every month**: 18:00 UTC in UK summer time, 19:00 UTC otherwise. On that day:
1. Every server must update. Clients on the new build can't join old servers because the protocol number changes (2633 → 2634 in October).
2. Oxide must update the same day, because it ships patched game DLLs. 2.0.7783 came out within hours on 1 Oct, followed by hotfix builds.
3. Plugins that used game code Facepunch changed stop compiling and unload.

Real examples from Oxide's own patch manifest:
- **September (2633):** `ItemContainer.CanAcceptItem` and `PlayerInventory.CanWearItem/CanEquipItem` gained a player parameter, and the `OnComposterUpdate` hook was removed.
- **October (2634):** `ItemContainer.Insert/Remove` gained a player parameter, and new Gen2 livestock animals arrived with their own hooks.

**Server rules (Facepunch's Community Server Guidelines, updated 15 Jul 2025).**
- Servers that change gameplay must be listed as **Modded**. Oxide does this by default (`"Modded": true`) and warns at startup when it's off.
- You may charge fees, take donations and sell cosmetics.
- You may **not** give players paid Facepunch DLC they don't own, pretend to be an official server, or circumvent paid content.

**Safety.** Oxide plugins aren't sandboxed. A plugin can read files, open network connections or start programs with the server's rights. That's why every Cyrus plugin goes through a strict static check before anyone sees it.

---

# Valheim in Cyrus: readiness checklist (2026-10-08)

Status: **`soon`** (not flipped; going `live` is the owner's call). Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-valheim`.

## What is done
- [x] `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.ts`: verified `GameSupport` (versions 1.0.x current / 0.221.x legacy / older unsupported, install side + plain-language reasons, breakage risks, outdated signals, 12 universal categories, sources, unknowns) and `VALHEIM_TARGET` (game line 1.0, network 40, BepInExPack 5.4.2351, Jötunn 2.30.2).
- [x] `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.knowledge.ts`: Valheim 1.0 knowledge pack (`GameSupport.knowledge`): ~28 verified API facts + 11 failure rules with regex detectors; `apiLinesFor()` for selective retrieval.
- [x] Generator `lib/cyrus/engine/games/valheim.ts` upgraded for 1.0 (see the report for the fixed bugs), version-aware (`cyrus.json`, startup version check), Thunderstore-correct manifest, Jötunn version enforcement for content mods, AI disclosure, runnable xUnit project for Yakko.
- [x] Validator `lib/cyrus/games/valheim.validate.ts` + tests `test/cyrus-game-valheim.test.ts`.
- [x] Compile harness `tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/` (node-2): every template compiled against the real 1.0.16 dedicated-server assemblies + generated tests run.

## Before Valheim can go live
### Must have
1. **Real AI generation path.** Today non-Minecraft games stream *template* code (`lib/cyrus/engine`), not model output. A real Valheim build needs the build service to accept `game: "valheim"`: a C# worker on the build VM with the .NET 8 SDK, the knowledge pack in the prompt (`apiLinesFor` on the plan), the validator as the safety scan, and `dotnet build` against the game assemblies as the compile step. (Build-VM changes are owner-only.)
2. **Game assemblies on the build host, never redistributed.** The harness downloads the free dedicated server's `Managed/*.dll` from Steam (app 896660, anonymous, public) at build time into a node-2 cache. The owner should confirm this is acceptable for a commercial build pipeline (it is how the repo's NxeonDevAdmin plugin is already built). Nothing proprietary is committed.
3. **Load test in a real server.** A throwaway Valheim dedicated server (Docker `lloesche/valheim-server` with `BEPINEX=true`, already used by Nxeon) on node-2 or a sandbox VM: install the DLL + Jötunn, start, grep `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` for `<Name> v1.0.0 loaded`, no Harmony errors, and for content mods that ZNetScene registered the prefab. Then a headless client check is not possible; client-side mods (HUD, music, grading) need one manual PC test per archetype.
4. **End-to-end customer test on a real Nxeon Valheim server**: generate → validate → install via the Mods tab (`lib/mods/installers/valheim.ts`, plugin folder `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/<Ns>-<Name>`) → restart → join with r2modman carrying the same mod → verify the feature in game → disable → confirm the removal warning was shown. Owner/test account only.
5. **Client-install guidance in the UI** (lifecycle/studio agents): show `cyrus.json.install.note` on the install card; for `side: both`, offer a download of the mod zip and an r2modman profile code for players; warn "console players will not be able to join" when the server has crossplay on.
6. **icon.png (256x256)** for the Thunderstore zip: the generator does not create one; the listing flow must add the creator's icon or the compact Cyrus badge.

### Should have
7. **Version table maintenance.** After every Valheim patch: `CYRUS_VH_REFRESH=1 devhost run --lock -- bash tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/run.sh`; if green, bump `VALHEIM_TARGET.game/verifiedBuild` and (when released) `bepinexPack`/`jotunn`; if red, add a failure rule and fix the generator. Cadence seen: major engine upgrades 2024-04 (Unity 2022), 2025-08 (Unity 6, 0.221.3), 2026-09 (1.0); small patches every 1 to 3 weeks after 1.0.
8. **Outdated watcher** (lifecycle agent): poll Thunderstore for BepInExPack_Valheim / Jötunn and Steam for app 896660 build changes; mark installed Cyrus mods "may need an update" when the game line moves, and tell creators (`outdatedSignals`).
9. **Golden examples** (research item 3): 3 to 5 hand-checked Valheim mods, compiled + load-tested, used as few-shot context and regression tests.
10. **Eval suite** (designed, not run, cost rule): 30 prompts across the 12 categories + 10 adversarial (network, file deletion, admin list, cheats) scored on validator pass, compile pass, load pass.

### Nice to have
11. Asset pipeline for custom models/textures (Unity AssetBundles built with the matching Unity 6 editor; Unity licence terms not checked yet; see research RENDERS-AND-TEXTURES.md).
12. ServerSync-style config locking so server admins' config wins over clients (Jötunn `AdminOnly` config entries are the lighter option).

## Owner decisions
- Accept downloading the public dedicated-server DLLs at build time for compile checks (never shipped)?
- AI disclosure text: generated mods say "created with the assistance of generative AI (Nxeon Cyrus)" in README/csproj, as Thunderstore requires. OK to name only Cyrus and its model names?
- Should Cyrus allow publishing Valheim mods to Thunderstore at all? Its rules reject "untested or non-functional AI-generated mods"; recommend: only after the load test (step 3) passes, and never auto-publish.
- Content mods force Jötunn (for version enforcement). Accept the extra dependency for players?

content.thinking:
Since the health endpoint only returns routing config and not the tier mapping, I should show the admin view sourced from the documented defaults in route.js, labeled clearly as "service defaults (from source, not read from the running service)," and separately derive an "observed" mapping by grouping the actual resolvedModel values from build records by their meta model — keeping the distinction between declared and observed honest.

For pricing and margin, I'll pull PRICES from usage.js and cross-reference token reservations (model, charged tokens, costUsd) to compute cost versus a revenue-equivalent figure at the top-up rate of 120 tokens per dollar, clearly labeling this as an approximation since granted tokens don't actually generate revenue. I also need to pull per-build charged tokens from the ledger spend delta or reservation.charged, and track queue depth from health.queued.

For error monitoring, I'm identifying builds stuck in non-terminal states over 30 minutes, failures with unreachable/lost/unavailable error codes in the past 24 hours, stale held reservations, settlement mismatches where a reservation is held but the build is terminal, service unreachability, and open report counts, plus a percentile function for p95 build time.

For canceling a build, I'm working through the logic for calling the service cancel endpoint and syncing the build, then figuring out how an admin force-fail should work when the service is unreachable—specifically how to mark the row failed and release tokens without charging the full cost, since the standard chargeCancelled config would charge in full, which isn't right for an admin-initiated cancellation of a stuck build.

I'm settling on marking the row failed with an "admin_cancelled" error code and running it through the normal token settlement path, where a zero cost naturally resolves to a zero charge, accepting a minor quirk where this still counts toward the free-failure tally. Then I'm designing a refund action using creditTokens with a refund kind and a per-build idempotency key, allowing a partial refund amount up to what was charged, while making sure it can't be issued more than once per build.

For undoing a refund, I'm planning to use revokeTokens scoped to just that refund's lot, so only unspent refund tokens get reversed, and giving the refund lot the same expiry window as an admin grant. For re-running a build, I'm thinking through using createModBuild with a baseBuildId and changeRequest for change-build re-runs, noting rate limits are keyed per user and that gateBuild will charge the customer's own tokens for the re-run, which seems appropriate when the customer requested it.

I'll add a confirmation checkbox so the admin acknowledges the re-run incurs real AI cost and spends the customer's tokens, with the action audited. Since the dev environment doesn't have the build service configured, createModBuild would just fail as "unavailable" and release the tokens, so I'm considering whether to run the mock service as its own process to actually exercise this path, similar to how v5 handled seeding through syncBuild, or whether to just rely on unit/DB-level checks for verifying cancel and re-run given time constraints.

For the users and tokens tab, I'm planning per-user search by email showing balance, plan, grants, ledger, comps, abuse signals, rate-limit status, and suspension, with my own actions calling creditTokens/revokeTokens directly rather than the existing redirect-based admin actions so I can audit and redirect back to the user's page; comp tier override reuses the existing upsert pattern since it's just an account field, not money. content.content:
### Cyrus v5: the owner's redesign (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v5`)

The owner's own Cyrus redesign (handoff `/tank/handoffs/cyrus/cyrus-handoff/`, START-HERE.md) replaces the v4 studio at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** (+ `/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`, and the core gallery at **`/dashboard/cyrus/cores`**). Same preview gate (`requireModBuilderUser()` on every page, `modBuilderUser()` on every API). The portal sidebar and top bar stay; the studio fills the app frame.

**Where it lives.** UI `components/cyrus/{chrome,cosmos,cores,icons,preview,prompt}` + `CyrusApp.tsx` (handoff components, imports re-rooted); state/engine `lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,data,types,camera,hooks,zip,highlight}.ts` + `lib/cyrus/engine/` (template generators); game logos `public/cyrus/games/`. Kept from v4: `components/cyrus/kit/` (icon set used by the token modal, the install-to-server modal), `lib/cyrus/{projects,meta,models,estimate,uploads,diff,tokens/}`.

**Scoping (nothing leaks into the portal).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/layout.tsx` wraps every Cyrus route in `.cyrus-root.nx-dark-island` and loads Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono as CSS variables on that box only. `studio.css` (handoff globals + network CSS) and `cores/cores.css` are generated from the handoff with every selector under `.cyrus-root`, keyframes and `@property` renamed `cy5-*`, and the three class names that collide with portal globals renamed (`cy5-glass`, `cy5-btn-ghost`, `cy5-kbd`). The root uses `container-type: size; contain: layout paint`, so the handoff's `position: fixed` chrome is contained in the content area; `100vw/vh` became `cqw/cqh`. Tailwind colour tokens are `cy-*` (`text-cy-ink`, `border-cy-line` …, `@theme inline` in `app/globals.css` pointing at variables that exist only on `.cyrus-root`), plus a `cy-light:` variant. `nx-dark-island` keeps the portal's generated light-mode retargeting off the studio (it has its own light theme). `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a studio selector is unscoped or a keyframe isn't `cy5-`.

**Theme.** The portal's: `html[data-theme="light"]` / localStorage `nx-theme`. The studio's toggle presses the portal's own toggle button; `useCyrusBoot` mirrors `data-theme` into the store for the canvas and shaders. No `cyrus-theme` key.

**Real vs template.** Minecraft is the one real game (`GAMES[].real`). The account's builds are its Minecraft mods (`lib/cyrus/real.ts deriveReal`: one mod per project, builds = versions, category from the build's own words, at most two extra category branches). Minecraft seeds are dashed **ideas**: clicking one writes a buildable prompt. Notes / restore / favourite are the existing `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`; files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`; downloads are the real `.jar` / source zip; **Deploy** opens the v4 install modal. Every other game (and added games) is the handoff's template generator, labelled "Template preview", spends no tokens, kept in localStorage per account (`cyrus-state-v1:<userId>`).

**Forge stream** (`POST /api/cyrus/generate`, NDJSON, handoff §6 GenEvents). A prompt that routes to Minecraft, or a change to a real mod, goes through `lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild` (extracted from `POST /api/mod-builder/builds`, which now calls it too: same validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap and token gate); token errors answer JSON 402/403/429 before the stream so `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError` opens the modal. Then `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` streams the real build: stage changes → `think`, the service `/live` draft → `file`/`chunk`, in-place edits → `file-set`, keep-alive `ping`, final source + `done {tokens: charged}` or `error`. `GET ?follow=<id>` re-attaches (page load with a running build, dropped connection; the client retries 4×). Template games run the handoff's `forgeStream()` (no model call). Additive event types: `build`, `file-set`, `ping`.

**Tokens** (UI-CONTRACT.md): `<CyrusTokensHost/>` in `CyrusApp`; `<CyrusTokenChip compact/>` replaces the handoff's credit counter in the top bar; `<CyrusTokenEstimate/>` in the prompt dock for real targets; `<CyrusModelLock/>` + typical token range per model + `<CyrusModelPanelFoot/>` in the model picker; `cyrusTokens.refresh()` after each real build. The local `credits` counter is gone. Model ids/names stay the economy's: Katara / Saka / Yakko.

### Cyrus token economy (2026-10-07, branch `feature/cyrus-tokens`)

Customers pay for Cyrus's AI in **Cyrus tokens**. Design and every number with its reasoning: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-economy/ECONOMY.md`. **Preview-only until launch:** Setting `cyrus_tok_live=false` means only private-preview accounts (`lib/preview-access.ts` "modbuilder") earn grants, see the checkout line, the balance or the plans. Everyone else sees and earns nothing (`lib/cyrus/tokens/access.ts tokensActiveFor`, fails closed). Cyrus is labelled **Beta · Minecraft Java only** wherever tokens appear.

**Unit.** 1 token = $0.002 of the build service's measured `costUsd` (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd=500`), times a model multiplier (Katara 1, Saka 1, Yakko 1.25), min 5 per build that reached the AI. Typical builds: Katara ~34 tokens (ChunkMirror 80), Saka ~52 (complex ~95; Sonnet-5 tier builds 150-338), Yakko ~214 simple. Customers never see a USD figure per token or a model family name (`test/cyrus-tokens-economy.test.ts`).

**Where tokens come from.**
- **Game servers**: on purchase `clamp(round5(100 + 16 x monthly $), 150, 750)`, on every paid renewal `clamp(round5(25 + 6 x monthly $), 40, 300)`; monthly $ = what was actually paid per month. Prepaid N-month terms earn per month (cap 12). Lots expire after 90 days (or term + 30 d). $0 trial starts earn the initial grant on the first paid renewal. Idempotent `gs:<serverId>:initial` / `gs:<serverId>:renew:<periodStartISO>`. Abuse caps: 3 initial grants per account per 30 days, 3,000 unexpired server tokens held. **Only games Cyrus builds for earn** (and get the checkout line): the server's game family must be a `status: "live"` game in `lib/cyrus/games.ts` (`lib/cyrus/tokens/games.ts earnsCyrusTokens`), today Minecraft Java only (`minecraft`; `bedrock` and other games earn nothing). Making a game live there makes its servers earn. `lib/cyrus/games.ts` on this branch is a byte-identical copy of the file on `feature/cyrus-modbuilder` (commit c19b512f86), so the two merge cleanly; if that file changes before the merge, take the modbuilder version. Hooks: `lib/game-order.ts placeGameOrder` (post-commit, `safeGrantPurchase`), `worker/billing.ts commitRenewal` (the single "renewed" exit, every sweep/card/PayPal/admin path) and `lib/actions.ts renewNow` (`safeGrantRenewal`). Never throws into an order or renewal.
- **Plans** (Stripe Billing subscriptions, monthly): Katara $4.99 = 750 tokens/month (Katara), Saka $19.99 = 3,500 (Katara, Saka), All models $49.99 = 10,000 (all three). Every paid invoice grants (`plan:<invoiceId>`), so renewals stack; each month's plan tokens last 3 months from their grant (`cyrus_tok_plan_rollover_months`), so at most 3 months stack. (A first design trimmed to "3 x the current plan" on each invoice; a real test-mode run showed a replayed old invoice could then expire paid tokens, so the cap is by age.) Upgrade = immediate proration (`always_invoice`, tokens in proportion to the money collected); downgrade = at the next renewal; cancel = at period end, plan tokens stay 30 days (Katara only) then expire; past_due keeps the unlock 3 days. Refunds (`charge.refunded`) take back that purchase's unspent tokens pro rata.
- **Top-ups**: one-off Checkout payment, $5-$100, 120 tokens/$, 12-month expiry, no unlock (`topup:<sessionId>`).
- **Admin**: grant / revoke / comp a tier at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`.

**Models.** No plan = Katara only; Katara plan = Katara; Saka plan = Katara + Saka; All models = all three; admin comp can raise it. Enforced server-side in `POST /api/mod-builder/builds` (403 `model_locked`).

# Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

- **2026-10-07 — Cyrus token economy (preview-only).** Tokens tied to real AI cost (1 token = $0.002, Yakko x1.25), game-server grants on purchase + every renewal scaled by price, Stripe plans (Katara $4.99 / Saka $19.99 / All models $49.99, monthly, stacking; each month's tokens last 3 months), custom top-ups, an append-only idempotent ledger with reserve -> settle -> release per build, server-side model unlocks, the Cyrus balance chip / plans / history UI, a gated game-checkout line and `/admin/cyrus-tokens`. Additive: `CyrusTokenAccount`, `CyrusTokenLot`, `CyrusTokenLedger`, `CyrusTokenReservation`, `CyrusPlan`. See "Cyrus token economy".

### Cyrus admin portal: /admin/cyrus (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v6-admin`, NOT deployed)

The staff side of Cyrus in one place. **URL-only during the private preview** (no admin-nav entry, like `/admin/mod-builder`): the real signed-in account must be staff AND on the `modbuilder` preview list (`preview_access_emails_modbuilder`), else 404. Each tab and each write maps to an admin Area (`lib/cyrus/admin/perms.ts`): **fleet** (ADMIN) Overview, Builds, Library & safety, cancel / re-run; **billing** (BILLING + ADMIN) Users & tokens, refunds, grants, comps; **support** (SUPPORT + ADMIN) Community moderation and suspensions; **platform** (ADMIN) Games & models, networking review + kill switch, Audit & settings. A role only sees its tabs; a support or billing account opening `/admin/cyrus` lands on its first tab. The older `/admin/cyrus-tokens`, `/admin/cyrus-mods` and `/admin/mod-builder` pages are unchanged.

**Tabs.**
- **Overview** (`/admin/cyrus`): builds per day (30 d, by outcome; refusals and cancels counted apart from failures), success / fail / refused rates and avg / p95 build time by game and by model, queue depth from the service `/health`, a "Needs attention" list (builds running > 30 min, lost contact with the builder in 24 h, token holds left after a build finished, service down, open reports), and **AI cost vs tokens charged by model** from settled holds, valued at the top-up price and at the cheapest plan price (worst case). It is a reference margin: granted tokens earn nothing directly, the page says so.
- **Builds** (`/admin/cyrus/builds`, `/admin/cyrus/builds/<id>`): search by id, plugin, prompt or customer email; filter by outcome, model, game, period. Detail: prompt and change request, stages and events, AI calls (internal model names and cost), usage per stage (live from the service, 0.5+ only), safety findings, files, token hold / charge / refund and ledger rows, the project's versions. Actions: **cancel** (service cancel; "force" fails it locally when the builder is unreachable, then the normal settle runs), **refund tokens** (`creditTokens` kind `refund`, idempotent key `admin-refund:<buildId>`, at most what the build was charged, one per build) and **undo refund** (`revokeTokens` limited to that refund's lot, never below zero), **re-run** (the same request through `createModBuild` for the customer: a real build with AI cost and a normal token hold, confirm box required).
- **Users & tokens** (`/admin/cyrus/users?u=<email or id>`): list view with suspended accounts, safety refusals in 30 d, token accounts, comped tiers. Account view: balance / held / available, model tier and comp, plan, abuse flags derived from real rows (refusals, fail rate, daily cap reached, reports against posts, hidden posts, written-off cost), rate limits (24 h token cap vs used, builds running / last hour / last minute vs the code limits 2 / 20 / 3), grant / revoke / comp forms (the economy path), suspension, lots and ledger.
- **Games & models** (`/admin/cyrus/games`): status per game from `lib/cyrus/games.ts` with a Setting override `cyrus_game_<id>_status` = live | soon | disabled (`lib/cyrus/game-status.ts`). **Live is only allowed for a game with a real build pipeline** (`CYRUS_BUILDABLE_GAMES`, Minecraft today); a stored "live" for any other game is ignored. Disabled = `createModBuild` refuses new builds for it (503 `game_disabled`); existing mods are untouched. Readiness checklists parsed from `docs/cyrus/readiness/<id>.md` (snapshots of the game agents' READINESS.md; `CYRUS_READINESS_DIR` points at the live notes in dev). Model table: Katara / Saka / Yakko to the service's source defaults (`MB_TIER_*`), models observed in 30 d of build records, list prices, token multiplier, hold ranges, average AI cost. Read-only service configuration: every `/health` field through a whitelist (no secrets) and the 0.5 efficiency knobs with their running values when reported.
- **Community** (`/admin/cyrus/community`): reports queue (hide with reason / dismiss), hidden posts (unhide), takedowns of public pages (reason required, restore), recent remixes, creator suspensions, the **networking review queue** (mods whose latest version declares hosts: approve exactly those hosts / block / clear; a new host sends it back to review; decisions in Setting `cyrus_net_reviews`) and the global kill switch `cyrus_mod_networking_enabled` (turning on needs a confirm), plus a moderation log.
- **Library & safety** (`/admin/cyrus/library`): pattern library coverage by category and verification (reads the library index JSON next to the service when it exists), recent safety refusals, scan rules that fired (block / warn, 30 d), compat-watch alerts (dry-run rows included) and installed-mod health signals when the lifecycle tables exist.
- **Audit & settings** (`/admin/cyrus/audit`): every Cyrus admin action (this section's, with before / after, plus the older pages' `cyrus.tokens.*` / `cyrusmods.*` rows), filterable; then every Cyrus setting with its description, default, current value and owner branch (marked "not merged yet" until that code lands), inline edit with type validation (`lib/cyrus/admin/settings-catalog.ts`), confirm for risky switches, and a guard that keeps the editor's own email in the preview list.

**Writes** (`lib/actions-cyrus-admin.ts`): `requireArea(<action's area>)` + the preview list + not impersonating; audited to `AuditLog` (action `cyrus.admin.<action>`, category `cyrus_admin`, `target`, `detail` = JSON `{before, after, note}`); tokens move only through `lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts`; reversible where possible. **No schema change.** Suspensions are one Setting `cyrus_suspensions` (JSON; scopes `build` = `createModBuild` refuses with 403 `suspended`, `community` = posting, reporting and publishing refused in `lib/actions-cyrus-mods.ts`); both checks fail open on a DB error.

**Plugs into other v6 branches** without compile-time coupling (`lib/cyrus/admin/optional.ts`): lifecycle `CyrusCreatorAlert` / `CyrusModSignal` rows, the library index JSON, the capability manifest (`declaredNetwork` in `lib/cyrus/admin/networking.ts`, the one place to point at `lib/cyrus/capabilities.ts` on merge), service 0.5 usage records. Until they merge each panel says which branch it waits for.

**Tests**: `test/cyrus-admin.test.ts` (permissions per role, outcomes, percentile, per-day buckets, margin maths, filter parsing and the SQL filter shape, attention and abuse rules, game status safety, suspensions, settings validation, audit detail, readiness parser, health secret filtering, networking review, library reader).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

**cyrus-admin: paused early on your wrap-up instruction.** The code is committed, but it has only been typechecked. The unit tests have not passed yet, and nothing has been opened in a browser or screenshotted.

**Branch / commit:** `feature/cyrus-v6-admin` @ `cd1c6882ba` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-admin`). Committed with explicit `git add` paths. Not deployed. No production data touched. I never started a dev server, and none of my node-2 units are left running.

**Checks that ran (node-2, under the lock):**
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- The tests failed at import for all 3 files. That includes the two existing ones (`test/cyrus-tokens-economy.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-mods.test.ts`), so this looks like how tests get run, not my code. The `server-only` package throws when `lib/geo-ip.ts` pulls it in, because the run lacked the react-server condition. Under your one-run limit I did not retry; the retry command is in PAUSED.md.

**What I built:** `/admin/cyrus`. It is URL-only during the preview, like `/admin/mod-builder`: you must be staff and on the `modbuilder` preview list. Each role only sees its own tabs:
- ADMIN: everything.
- BILLING: Users & tokens only.
- SUPPORT: Community only.

| Tab | Shows today (real data) | Waits for |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | Builds per day; success / fail / refused rates by game and model; average and p95 build time; queue depth from `/health`; a needs-attention list (stuck builds, lost builder, leftover token holds, service down, reports); AI cost vs tokens charged, priced at the top-up rate and at the cheapest plan rate | Nothing |
| Builds + detail | Search and filters; prompt, stages, events, AI calls, safety findings, files, tokens. Actions: cancel (with a force option), refund tokens and undo refund (through the token ledger, one refund per build), re-run (a real build, confirm box) | Usage per stage needs build service 0.5 deployed |
| Users & tokens | Balance, ledger, grants, plan, comps (the earlier ones included), abuse flags, rate limits; grant / revoke / comp; suspend from building and/or community | Nothing |
| Games & models | Status per game with a settings override `cyrus_game_<id>_status`. Only Minecraft can be set live, because it is the only game with a real build pipeline. Disabled stops new builds. Readiness checklists, model mapping and observed models, read-only service knobs | The studio map reads the override after studio-ui passes it one prop. Terraria and Zomboid checklists show, but those games aren't registered yet |
| Community | Reports queue, hidden posts, takedowns / restore, recent remixes, suspensions, networking kill switch, moderation log | The networking review queue fills once the capabilities merge lands; remix disputes need the community merge |
| Library & safety | Recent safety refusals, which scan rules fired | Library coverage needs the library merge; compat-watch rows need the lifecycle merge |
| Audit & settings | Every Cyrus admin action with before/after (older Cyrus admin pages' actions included); every Cyrus setting with description and default, validated inline edits, confirm on risky switches | Nothing |

**How it is built:**
- Every write checks the role, writes an audit row, and is reversible where possible. Tokens move only through `lib/cyrus/tokens/ledger.ts`.
- No schema change: the audit goes into the existing `AuditLog`; suspensions, network reviews and game status are Settings.
- Small hooks in shared files:
  - `lib/modbuilder/create.ts` refuses new builds for suspended accounts and disabled games.
  - `lib/actions-cyrus-mods.ts` refuses posts, reports and publishing from suspended accounts.
- Docs: a section "Cyrus admin portal: /admin/cyrus" with a short admin guide, plus a change-history bullet.
- `docs/cyrus/readiness/*.md` are snapshot copies of the game agents' READINESS files. Refresh them at merge.

**Files:** `app/admin/cyrus/**`, `components/admin/cyrus/ui.tsx`, `lib/cyrus/admin/*`, `lib/cyrus/{game-status,game-status.server,suspensions}.ts`, `lib/actions-cyrus-admin.ts`, `test/cyrus-admin.test.ts`.

**Left to do** (exact steps in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/admin/PAUSED.md`):
1. Re-run the tests with the react-server condition.
2. Run the prepared, uncommitted harness in `.cyrus-admin-verify/`: fake seed data, a mock `/health`, and a Playwright script that does the UI actions, screenshots every tab (dark and light, 1440 and 390) and checks SUPPORT's access. Then `devhost stop all`.

**Decisions for the owner:**
- Should SUPPORT staff see build prompts? (Today they can't; only ADMIN sees builds.)
- Should "re-run" exist at all? It spends real AI money and holds the customer's tokens.
- Which price should the margin use as the main figure: top-up rate or plan rate?
